source.description: Project file-input entry that opens the attacker-controlled XML file through the text reader API.

sink.description: Second free of id->name when the reader frees the document ID table.

root_cause.description: Ownership of attr->name is moved into id->name without clearing attr->name, leaving both the attribute and ID table to free the same string.

taint_source.description: The reader opens the PoC-backed XML file. The harness only creates the temporary file; libxml2 consumes it here.

tainted_value_origin.description: The parser materializes an attacker-controlled XML attribute name as heap-owned attr->name.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled XML file is opened through the text reader.
XML parsing reaches a start tag and SAX attribute handling.
The attribute name is copied into attr->name.
ID removal aliases attr->name into id->name without clearing attr->name.
Document ID-table cleanup frees id->name, the same pointer, again.

fine_trace.note: SAX start-element handling creates an XML attribute from attacker-controlled markup.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: ASan allocation context: the attribute name string is duplicated into heap storage.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: During reader node cleanup, ID attributes are removed from the document ID table before the attribute itself is freed.

grounding.evidence: No sanitizer or patch artifact directly grounded this step.

fine_trace.note: Root cause: id->name aliases attr->name, but attr->name remains non-NULL and still owned by the attribute.

grounding.evidence: Step is on a changed patch line or a patch hunk line with a patch-groundable role.

fine_trace.note: First free: attribute cleanup frees cur->name after the pointer was copied into id->name.
When the reader is destroyed, the document ID table is freed.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

fine_trace.note: ASan crash location: the ID table frees the same name pointer that xmlTextReaderFreeProp already freed.

grounding.evidence: Step file/line appears in sanitizer crash_stack.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The XML reader parses attacker-controlled markup and creates an attribute name string in attr->name. During reader cleanup, xmlTextReaderRemoveID() removes an ID attribute from the ID table by assigning id->name = attr->name, but it does not clear attr->name. xmlTextReaderFreeProp() then frees cur->name, while the ID table still holds the same pointer. Later xmlTextReaderFreeDoc() frees the ID table and xmlFreeID() frees id->name again, causing a double-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch sets attr->name = NULL immediately after assigning id->name = attr->name. This makes ownership transfer explicit: attribute cleanup no longer frees the transferred pointer, and the ID table frees it exactly once.
